methodology_note: Bank: residual income (cash earnings less after-tax one-offs, less a cost-of-equity charge on opening tangible book) discounted at the AUD cost of equity, plus opening tangible book, plus a Gordon terminal on Y5 residual income. Deposits are operating funding, so net debt is zero and no owner-FCF DCF is built. Same family as BEN.AX and ANZ.AX (residual income on TBV), SRBK and SOFI.

valuation_philosophy.methodology: Residual income on tangible book value, discounted at cost of equity -- a bank model, NOT an owner-FCF DCF
valuation_philosophy.rationale: Bank of Queensland is an APRA-regulated authorised deposit-taking institution. Its operating cash flow (-A$1.2bn FY22, +A$3.6bn FY23, -A$0.9bn FY24, +A$2.3bn FY25) is loan, deposit and liquid-asset flow, not owner earnings; deposits (A$75.7bn) and borrowings (A$16.7bn, which include the A$660m Capital Notes 2/3 and covered bonds) are the raw material of net interest income, not net debt. The economically meaningful question is whether the bank earns more than its cost of equity on the tangible capital shareholders have in it -- and BOQ has not since FY19 (cash ROTE 9.4% FY22, 8.6% FY23, 7.1% FY24, 7.9% FY25, 7.4% 1H26 against a ~10.5% cost of equity). Intrinsic equity = opening tangible book (A$4,587m est. at 31-Aug-26 after the capital return) + PV of residual income (cash earnings less one-offs less CoE x opening TBV) over five years + PV of a Gordon terminal on year-5 residual income. Per-share values divide by 628.3m shares (658.1m less ~29.9m assumed bought back).
valuation_philosophy.wacc_field_note: The 'wacc' field in every scenario is the COST OF EQUITY in AUD, not a blended WACC. Built as AGB 10-year ~4.3% + beta ~1.12 x Australian ERP ~5.5% = ~10.5% base. Half a point above the BEN.AX rate (10.0%) because BOQ carries two Court Enforceable Undertakings (APRA and AUSTRAC), a 66.5% cost-to-income ratio, a CEO transition and a retail franchise whose own goodwill was written to zero in FY25. Franking credits are ignored in base and bear; bull credits roughly half the ~1.5pp franking benefit via a 9.5% CoE.
valuation_philosophy.terminal_value_note: Terminal value is a Gordon perpetuity on year-5 residual income at 'terminal_growth'. In base and bear the year-5 residual income is NEGATIVE (ROTE 9.5% / 7.5% against CoE 10.5% / 11.0%), so the terminal is a deduction from tangible book and a higher growth rate LOWERS value -- read the sensitivity matrix with that in mind. Growth is set at the rate the scenario's capital base compounds (base ~2%: 72% payout on a ~9% ROTE retains ~2.5% of TBV a year, less continued capital recycling; bear 1%: an 80% payout on a 7% ROTE retains ~1.4%). The implied exit P/TBV (terminal equity / Y5 TBV) is reported per scenario and checked against BOQ's own FY22-FY25 balance-date P/TBV range of 0.74-0.98x and today's 0.92x.
valuation_philosophy.timing_note: Periods are fiscal years (September-August) from an ESTIMATED 31-Aug-2026 tangible book (Y1 = FY27), each discounted as a full year from the 21-Sep-2026 valuation date. FY26 closed three weeks before the valuation date and the annual report is not yet published (due ~mid-October 2026), so the Y0 balance is the audited 31-Aug-2025 TBV rolled forward by estimated FY26 statutory profit, the three dividends paid in FY26 and the assumed buyback. Refresh the anchors when the FY26 annual report lands.

inputs.share_count_basis: 658.119m ordinary shares net of treasury shares at 31-Aug-25 (FY2025 annual report line 8510; 661.469m issued less ~3.4-4.0m treasury shares held for employee plans, line 10556-10567), less an ASSUMED 29.9m shares bought back on-market at ~A$6.70 (A$200m) as the balance of the ~A$300m Challenger capital return, giving 628.3m. The DRP is satisfied by on-market purchase (no discount; 9% participation), so it does not add shares; ~A$8-9m/yr of equity-settled SBC is expensed inside cash earnings and the share count is otherwise held FLAT. Diluted WANOS of 753m includes ~88m shares from Capital Notes 2 and 3 whose distributions are already deducted from profit -- counting them as shares too would double-count -- and 10.8m anti-dilutive options.
inputs.net_debt_note: Zero by construction: deposits (A$75.7bn) and borrowings (A$16.7bn incl. covered bonds, senior unsecured, A$886m Tier 2 and A$660m AT1 Capital Notes 2/3) are operating funding for a bank, not net debt. The residual-income flow is already after all funding and AT1 distribution costs, so nothing is subtracted from equity value.
inputs.goodwill_and_intangibles_note: Goodwill 397 (BOQ Business CGU only; Retail Bank goodwill of 170 impaired to nil in FY25), customer intangibles/brands 25, computer software 460, assets under construction 107, OMB right-to-operate 54 (FY2025 AR intangibles note line 10640). BOQ's own ROTE definition deducts ALL intangibles, so tangible book here does too. Intangibles are assumed flat over the projection (software capitalisation ~= amortisation); FY24-FY25 they fell 1,162 -> 1,043 on the impairment.
inputs.at1_note: The ME Bank AT1 'other equity instruments' were redeemed in FY24 (A$100m); Capital Notes 2 and 3 (A$660m AT1) are classified in Borrowings, so total equity of A$5,907m is ordinary shareholders' equity with no AT1 deduction required.

tbv_roll_forward_to_aug26.note: FY26 statutory NPAT estimate = 1H26 actual A$136m + 2H26E A$149m (cash ~A$182m less ~A$33m non-cash: residual whole-of-loan sale items guided at -A$45-55m total of which -A$31m was booked in 1H26, plus ~A$8m branch strategy). Dividends paid in FY26: FY25 final 20c (ex 28-Oct-25), FY26 interim 20c (ex 4-May-26) and a 15c SPECIAL (ex 13-Aug-26, ~A$99m, the first tranche of the Challenger capital return; the A$6.70 price is ex this dividend, so it is NOT added to value). Reserve movements and net intangible capitalisation assumed nil. Remaining ~A$200m of the announced ~A$300m return assumed executed as an on-market buyback at ~A$6.70 in early FY27 and treated as a t=0 adjustment; if it is not executed, TBV/share is A$7.27 on 658.1m shares and every scenario IV moves by less than A$0.05.

inputs.dividend_per_share_annual_note: FY25 38c (18c + 20c); FY26 run-rate 40c (20c interim declared April 2026 + 20c assumed final) plus the 15c special paid August 2026
inputs.last_fcf_basis: NOT owner FCF: bank model. This is FY25 cash earnings after tax (A$383m), the last audited earnings base; FY26E is ~A$358m (1H26 A$176m actual, -4% YoY). Cash ROTE 7.9% FY25 on average tangible equity of ~A$4,860m; 7.4% in 1H26. Owner FCF is undefined for a deposit taker.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report: equity-settled share-based payments ~A$9m (treasury-share net acquisitions A$9m in financing cash flow; 10.8m options and ~7m award rights outstanding). Already expensed inside cash earnings; no separate deduction.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not applicable: interest income (A$5,054m FY25) IS the revenue of a bank; nothing is stripped
inputs.buyback_note: Assumed A$200m on-market buyback (balance of the ~A$300m Challenger capital return after the A$99m special dividend paid 13-Aug-26). The split and final size were 'subject to market conditions, Board and regulatory approvals' at 1H26; confirm against the FY26 annual report. Historically BOQ has bought back only A$3-17m/yr for employee-plan treasury shares.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-21T06:10:29Z (16:10 AEST, ASX regular close incl. closing auction)
inputs.balance_sheet_date_note: Latest FILED balance sheet in the folder is 31-Aug-2025 (FY2025 annual report); the 1H26 file is the results presentation, which carries ROTE/CET1 but no balance sheet. Y0 tangible book is rolled forward to an estimated 31-Aug-2026 -- see tbv_roll_forward_to_aug26.
inputs.balance_sheet_source: BOQ.AX_Annual_FY2025.txt (balance sheet lines 7363-7404; intangibles note 10628-10645; capital adequacy table 4851-4872; share capital note 10550-10567; ordinary shares line 8510; cash earnings reconciliation 3948-3960; key metrics 4180-4240; five-year summary 6420-6432 and 12575-12600). BOQ.AX_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt (1H26 key results lines 138-157; reconciliation 436-456; capital 668-695; Challenger guidance 701-727).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in AUD: Australian 10-year government bond ~4.3% (Sep-2026) + beta ~1.12 x Australian equity risk premium ~5.5% = ~10.5% base; 11.0% bear; 9.5% bull (partial franking credit). Set 0.5pp above BEN.AX (10.0%) for the two open Court Enforceable Undertakings (APRA Program rQ, AUSTRAC AML First; 61% of remedial activities complete at Feb-26), the A$50m APRA overlay, a 66.5% cost-to-income ratio, a new CEO and a retail CGU whose goodwill BOQ itself impaired to nil citing 'an increase in the discount rate'.
inputs.notes: MODEL: residual income on tangible book at cost of equity (dcf-methods routing table, row 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker, thrift'). Owner-FCF DCF rejected because OCF is loan/deposit flow and deposits are not net debt. First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry existed. Earnings base: FY25 statutory NPAT A$133m carries the A$170m Retail Bank goodwill impairment (non-cash, no TBV effect) and A$82m of after-tax branch-strategy, restructuring and Remedial Action Plan costs, so the ROTE path is anchored on cash ROTE (FY25 7.9%, 1H26 7.4%) and one-offs are charged explicitly below cash earnings rather than buried in the ROTE path. FY26 guidance (1H26, Apr-26): sub-inflation cost growth; NIM tailwinds in 2H26; commercial lending at/above system; home lending contraction easing with growth from FY27; LIE 'historically low experience may not persist'; Challenger transaction broadly cash-earnings neutral in FY26, cash ROE +15-25bps, non-cash items -A$45-55m; CET1 target 10.25-10.75%, payout 60-75%. Price is the ASX regular close; not an after-hours print.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Terminal growth of residual income, 2.0% base. Every historical growth series is negative or acquisition-distorted: the 5yr revenue (+8.7%) and equity (+6.9%) CAGRs are the FY21 ME Bank acquisition (A$1.35bn raise, balance sheet 57bn -> 91bn), not organic compounding; on a post-ME basis (FY22-FY25) revenue is -0.3%/yr, cash earnings -7.9%/yr, cash EPS -8.4%/yr, TBV/share -4.3%/yr and gross loans -1.4%/yr. 2.0% is below BEN.AX's 3.0% because BOQ's balance sheet is shrinking (mortgage run-off, A$3.7bn Challenger loan sale) rather than growing; the bank model has no revenue/FCF growth driver.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR (-4.0%) vs statutory EPS 3yr CAGR (-32.6%) diverge by far more than 30%: FY25 statutory EPS (20.1c) carries the A$170m Retail Bank goodwill impairment and A$82m of after-tax branch/restructuring/RAP costs, while FY22 EPS (63.1c) was a NIM peak (1.71%) at a 56.5% cost-to-income ratio. Neither end is a run-rate; the model is driven by ROTE on tangible book, anchored on FY25 cash ROTE 7.9% and 1H26 cash ROTE 7.4%.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are null by design: operating cash flow of a deposit-taking bank (-A$1.2bn FY22, +A$3.6bn FY23, -A$0.9bn FY24, +A$2.3bn FY25) is loan/deposit/liquid-asset flow, not owner earnings. Cash earnings fell 491 -> 450 -> 343 -> 383 over FY22-FY25 as NIM compressed 1.71% -> 1.56% -> 1.64% and cost-to-income rose 56.5% -> 66.8% -> 64.7%; TBV/share fell from A$8.44 (FY22) to A$7.39 (FY25) because payout ran at 60-66% of cash earnings while statutory profit was hit by A$0.5bn of cumulative non-cash items, and the FY23 A$200m ME integration/restructuring charges.

base.terminal_growth_label: perpetual growth of residual income after Y5 (negative RI in this scenario: higher growth lowers value)
base.rationale: Cash ROTE steps 7.9% -> 9.5% from FY26E's ~7.4%. FY27 gets the full-year Challenger benefit (+15-25bps ROE guided), a smaller capital base after the A$300m return, 2H26 NIM tailwinds (replicating portfolio, TD spreads) and the first ME-decommissioning/Capgemini savings, but the mortgage book is still shrinking and LIE normalises toward 8-10bps of GLA, so 7.9%. Cost-to-income drifts from 66.5% toward ~60% by FY30 as legacy platforms are switched off, lifting ROTE to 9.5% -- still 1pp BELOW the 10.5% cost of equity, because BOQ has not earned its CoE since FY19 and management withdrew its FY26 ROE 9.25% target. After-tax one-offs A$60m FY27 (residual whole-of-loan items, branch optimisation, RAP embed costs, legacy platform write-offs on decommissioning), A$40m/A$25m, then A$15m/yr. Payout 72% (FY25 65.6%; 1H26 20c on 26.8c cash EPS = 75%; target 60-75%). CoE 10.5%, residual-income growth 2.0% after Y5. With ROTE below CoE throughout, residual income is negative in every year and the equity is worth ~0.8x tangible book.

bull.terminal_growth_label: perpetual growth of residual income after Y5
bull.rationale: The 'simpler, specialist bank' lands: the digital platform (72% of retail customers and 75% of home-loan flow already digital) and ME decommissioning take cost-to-income from 66.5% to the mid-50s by FY30, NIM holds ~1.75% on a better funding mix post-Challenger, Business Bank keeps compounding 7-9% in healthcare/agri/commercial property at higher risk-adjusted returns, home lending returns to growth in FY27 as guided, and proportional-regulation reforms (Council of Financial Regulators) narrow the standardised-vs-IRB capital gap. ROTE reaches 11.5% by FY31 -- roughly BOQ's FY18-FY19 level and 2pp above a franking-adjusted 9.5% CoE. One-offs fade after FY27 (A$50m). Payout 65% as retained capital funds specialist lending growth. Implied exit ~1.3x TBV, where BOQ traded pre-ME (FY16-FY19 P/B ~1.2-1.5x) but not since.

bear.terminal_growth_label: perpetual growth of residual income after Y5 (negative RI: growth is the rate the sub-CoE capital base compounds)
bear.rationale: Status quo plus a penalty. Mortgage competition from the majors and ANZ-Suncorp plus RBA cuts compress NIM back toward 1.60% while the transformation savings are eaten by RAP, AML and compliance spend, so cost-to-income stays 65%+ and ROTE sits at 6.5-7.5% -- which is simply FY24-1H26 (7.1%/7.9%/7.4%) extended. AUSTRAC escalates the CEU to civil-penalty proceedings and a ~A$150m (non-deductible) penalty lands in FY28 on top of A$90m of FY27 transformation/RAP costs and A$40-60m/yr of continuing restructuring (A$90m/A$180m/A$60m/A$40m/A$40m after tax). The board defends the 40c dividend so payout rises to 80%, and LIE normalises to ~15bps in a softer housing market. CoE 11.0%, growth 1.0%. Residual income is deeply negative in every year and in perpetuity, so the equity is worth ~0.53x tangible book -- below the 0.74x BOQ bottomed at (FY23 balance date) and the 52-week low (5.91 = 0.81x), because the bear embeds a penalty and a permanent 3.5pp negative ROTE-CoE spread with no takeover.

entry_price.method: Price at which buying today, collecting the scenario's Y1-Y5 dividends and selling at the Y5 intrinsic equity value (TBV + terminal residual income at the scenario CoE) returns 15%/yr. Terminal value is at CoE, not at the hurdle.

required_return_table.note: Base ROTE/payout/one-off path re-discounted at each cost of equity (the equity charge moves with it), terminal growth 2%

sensitivity.axis_note: Rows = cost of equity (%), columns = perpetual growth of residual income after Y5 (%). Base-case ROTE, payout and one-off path. At a CoE of 10% or above the base Y5 residual income is negative, so value FALLS as growth rises (the 0% column holds the shortfall flat); at 8-9% the Y5 ROTE of 9.5% clears the CoE and the usual direction returns.

sensitivity_rote_vs_coe.axis_note: Rows = flat five-year ROTE (%), columns = cost of equity (%). Base one-offs, 72% payout, 2% terminal growth. At ROTE = CoE the value is tangible book less the PV of one-offs (~A$6.91/share at 10%/10%). Today's A$6.70 sits between the 9% and 10% ROTE rows at a 10% CoE and needs ~10.2% flat ROTE at the base 10.5% CoE -- i.e. the market already prices a fuller recovery than the base path delivers.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35; bear lifted to 30% and bull cut to 20%. The bear is essentially the current run-rate (cash ROTE 7.1-7.9% FY24-1H26, cost-to-income 66.5% and rising) plus an AUSTRAC penalty -- it needs nothing to go wrong that has not already been going wrong for four years, and BOQ carries two open Court Enforceable Undertakings, a A$50m APRA overlay, a CEO three months into the job and a retail franchise whose goodwill was written to nil. The bull requires BOQ to earn 11.5% ROTE, a level it last saw before the ME Bank acquisition, on a shrinking mortgage book, AND a franking-adjusted CoE. Base is a partial recovery that still never earns the cost of equity.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide: SBC (~A$9m, 0.5% of income) is expensed inside cash earnings and there is no SBC add-back to dispute, so the house/street band collapses and band_position is null.

key_metrics_reference.cash_rote_note: FY24, FY25 and 1H26 as reported; FY22 and FY23 derived as cash earnings / average (total equity less intangibles) from the balance sheets (FY22 491 on avg 5,223; FY23 450 on avg 5,243)

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
